utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Seric, thank you very much for providing us with the translation of the D2/72 and D2/73.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Your gratitude should be conveyed to the interpreters who managed to do it and provide it, with the help of Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Scott. Cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I note from your background as it's been explained to us that you studied history and archaeology at the philosophy faculty at the University of Zagreb from 1987 to 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this a period of continuous study, that is from 1987 to 1994?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had two breaks in between.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were those breaks and what was the nature of those breaks, please?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were between April 1992 until September 1992. That was the first time. And the second time was between July 1993 and May 1994. During that time, I was involved in the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only on the second occasion or on both occasions that you just gave us?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On both occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll come back to that, then. As a result of your studies, did you obtain any degrees?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am a graduate historian and archaeologist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say graduate and I understand educational systems sometimes vary between country to country and institution to institution, but when you say you graduated, does that mean you completed a three or four-year course of study as we might call in some places an undergraduate degree?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the end of a four-year study.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have any degrees after that, that is after the end of your four years? Did you continue and obtain any other degrees?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Currently I'm doing post-graduate studies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So we can understand, then, that at least at the present time, you have what we might consider an undergraduate degree in what, history?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you consider your actual expertise, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what you consider the field of my research?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war of -- history of war, warfare including theory, and more specifically, my narrow specialisation is World War II and the Patriotic War.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say the Patriotic War, which war are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the war in Croatia, and may I add, the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina during the same period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in terms of your expertise, then, let me follow up on that for a moment. Do you consider yourself primarily an historian then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I do not do archaeology any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you consider yourself a military analyst?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider yourself a political -- what some might call a political scientist, an expert on government and politics?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first place, I address military aspect of a period, and I analyse political issues only to the extent needed to explain the time or, rather, to present it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider yourself an intelligence expert?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I believe I'm quite familiar with the intelligence service of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that during two periods of time, if I heard you well, that you were a participant in some fashion in the war in the former Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the first time period that you gave us a few moments ago, can you tell the Judges, please, how it was that you were involved in that -- in those conflicts, if you had a unit assignment, what unit you were in, and what location in the former Yugoslavia were you assigned to?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of students platoon of the Livno Brigade called Petar Kresimir IV on both occasions. During the first interval, I was at the front around Livno, and the second time I was around Livno and Uskoplje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we might -- some of us might known Uskoplje better as Gornji Vakuf; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. It's a new term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were your duties? Can you give us a bit more help, please, on the exact time that you were engaged, excuse me, around Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three times. Ten days each. Ten days on every occasion. And I was assigned to the defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I understand ten days on each occasion, but can you help us in general? Are we talking about the summer of 1993 --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, three times and ten days on every occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm asking you, sir, about the period of time when that occurred. Was this in the summer of 1993, the fall of 1993? When were you assigned at Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: November 1993, December 1993, and now I'm not quite sure whether it was March or April 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was your commanding officer during that time?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What level do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what was the name of your unit again?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade -- well, I was in a platoon, and this platoon made part of the Petar Kresimir IV Livno Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Stjepan Sucic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this an HVO unit or an HV unit?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an HVO unit, reserve brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about command office your Mr. Susic, if I heard you correctly? Was he an HV officer or had he been an HV officer before taking command of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I believe he was an HVO officer. He was -- he came from Vukovar, but I believe he was born in Livno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you, sir, was whether he was an HV officer and you said yes, but then you described him as HVO. Had he been an HV officer?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at what point had he joined the HVO or at least engaged in service with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was a member of the brigade and specifically the platoon commander. It wasn't mine to ask questions like that. I mean, we didn't talk in that way. I never saw him in the papers referring to that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, we'll get into this perhaps -- in much more detail later, but you knew during your time of military service, probably on both occasions, didn't you, that a substantial number, majority of the senior HVO officers either were at the time or had been HV officers; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does the word "substantial" mean to you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More than a few.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than a few? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you engaged in any military service since ending that second term that you again described to us some minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was a professional soldier in the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when and where was that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: September 1994, August 1995, the 1st Guards Brigade of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 1st Guards Brigade of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljko Vlasanovic [As interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, sir, moving forward with your background, you tell us that spent some time at the central military archives. What is the central military archives?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the central archives of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where are those archives located, please?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the Ministry of Defence on Kralja Zvonimir street. In Zagreb, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this archive, if I can describe it this way, is it primarily a repository of documents, someplace, a collection perhaps of shelves and filing cabinets, or is it an active archives in the terms that the Ministry of Defence uses it on an active basis?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the latter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this an open or public archive? Can members of the public come off the street and look through this archive?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Croatia there is an Archive Act. For 30 years, nothing is accessible, until 30 years expires. The same thing applies to this archive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, except, sir, the fact that you've worked there. I assume you've had access to this material; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had the authorisation of the Defence Minister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for what purposes did you have this authorisation?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Scientific work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you employed by the Ministry of Defence at that time?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, in part. And in November or, rather, in October 2001, I quit the Ministry of Defence, that is, the Croatian Army. But the authorisation was still valid because of the project that had been launched by the government of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you've told the Chamber, then, is this is an archive of the Ministry of Defence, the Republic of Croatia, which is not generally open to the public or outsiders but that you have had access to this archive; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still have access to it now?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unless the new lady Minister has not withdrawn the authorisation of the previous Minister, then I do. But I'm not aware that she's done it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who is the director or person in charge of this archive at the present time?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Branko Mihaljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've also mentioned something called the military museum of the Ministry of Defence. I take it this is something different than the central military archive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is that located, please?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Vlaska street in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who owns or operates this museum?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Dinko Cutura.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the individual person. Should we understand that it's owned and operated by the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a museum of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is there? Museums, I suppose, can be all sorts of things. Is it a tourist museum or is it again a collection of documents or what is there?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They -- it displays exhibits from the patriotic -- from the homeland war. And by and large, one needs to announce himself previously and then he's allowed in. I mean, the museum is provisional. I mean, it is only its temporary location. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also been associated with something called the Croatian Institute of History. What is that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Central Croatian Historical Institution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who owns or operates the Croatian Institute of History?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Mirko Valentic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it again a creature, if you will, of the government of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who owns it and funds it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institute was established in the 1960s. It was set up by the League of Communists of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who owns --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is financed by the Ministry of Science of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it correct, sir, to try to move forward here a bit, that apart from your academic experience, all or virtually all of your vocational life and work since the early 1990s or even the late 1980s has been either in the military, of either Croatia or the HVO, or in association with some agency or project of the Croatian government? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was quite clear about how long I was with the HVO. Between November -- that is, October last year, that is for the past year I've been engaged in a project. And from the beginning of 2000, I was also involved in some projects of the government of the Republic of Croatia or the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, I won't belabour this too much, but it's correct, then, that apart from your education you have been -- and apart from your time in the HVO, you have been continuously employed by or associated with the government of Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institution -- yes. Mostly, yes. But the institution that I am with now is independent of the daily politics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you mentioned already something called the Croatian Information Service or HIS, we may have heard before, H-I-S. What were your duties in association with HIS?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the order of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia from April 1999 to early June 2000, I was an archives officer at the HIS, H-I-S.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the record is clear, HIS is what many of us would call an intelligence service of the Republic of Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the intelligence services of the Republic of Croatia to be exact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during this period of assignment to HIS, who was your superior? Who did you report to in connection with this project?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never submitted any report on my work to anyone. Formally speaking, I think my superior was the head of the HIS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, three persons held that job during that time. The first one, to be quite frank, I can't remember the name of that one. The second one was Miroslav Tudjman, and the third one was Ozren Zunec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man Miroslav Tudjman was the son of the late President Franjo Tudjman; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Zunec would be the head of HIS who was appointed after the change of governments when Stipe Mesic become president; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was after Stipe Mesic became president that documents in the Republic of Croatia in these archives and at the Ministry of Defence first began to become available to this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I allowed this set of questions and answers, but I object to any further examination in this direction, because I do not know whether my learned friend is trying to conduct a new investigation with the help of this expert witness or is it -- or whatever he's trying to establish, that is not going to discredit this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the question asked by the Prosecutor has some merits in it, and we also want to know the answer of that question. On the other hand, Mr. Scott, you really spend too much time on those questions. I hope you could get over this part of the cross-examination and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour. I can only represent to the Chamber that I believe it would be tied up in later questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in any event, sir, let me repeat the question. It was after Stipe Mesic became president that the documents in the Republic of Croatia in these archives and at the Ministry of Defence first began to become available to this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Partly, yes. I don't know what the cooperation before that was like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true, sir, that a substantial number of HVO documents had in fact been moved out of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the express purpose of keeping them from this Tribunal, hiding them in Croatia until the change of governments? And you know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott -- sorry. Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question. It has nothing to do with the substance of this examination. If we're going to be telling the truth, then the constitutional law on the cooperation with this Tribunal was signed by the HDZ government headed by the late President Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, very many times we have been warned that politics do not have a place in this court despite the political indictment and the political appearance of the Prosecutor at every moment. These are deliberate allegations by the Prosecutor, and this is just political propaganda on behalf of his witness, Mr. Mesic, who is available to this Prosecution whenever they want him to be available. I believe this is propaganda because he's now President Mesic called as a witness in the Milosevic case. I think this has nothing to do with the expert witness. Let's examine this witness on the things for which he has been called. He is not a fact witness. He is an expert witness. And Mr. Prosecutor has been doing things for a year that now I believe have become clear to all of us after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this topic has appeared many, many times during our proceedings, and this witness worked for a considerable time in that institution. And we also believe that the witness has the right to answer that question by yes or no. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree, but let's do that in the Prosecutor's office. The knowledge about the archives or whatever other knowledge that this witness has may be discussed in the Prosecutor's office, because what we are dealing with here is the indictment, and the indictment is something completely different. We are wasting time on something that Mr. Prosecutor can discuss with this witness after the hearing. We know what the indictment is. We know why this witness has been called. And if there is anything else that my learned friend wants to cause with him, why don't they discuss it after in the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have already said that this topic has been mentioned many, many times during our proceedings. We want to know how this witness knows about this matter. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that a substantial number of the documents that are now at the HVO archive were in fact moved out of Bosnia-Herzegovina by representatives of the Republic of Croatia for the express purpose of keeping that evidence from this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember having participated in any such activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't ask you whether you participated. I asked you what you know. You worked with this archive extensively. You worked with the head of one of the main Croatian intelligence agencies for some substantial period of time. Isn't it true, sir, that documents were concealed, spirited out of Bosnia-Herzegovina and concealed from this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question, to the way it has been asked. The Prosecutor is giving testimony instead of asking questions. Why can't my learned friend ask a concrete question without himself giving testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness has answered that question, and I think the Prosecutor has the right to ask a follow-up question, because we are not quite clear about the meaning of the answer of this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me state it again, sir. You did said that you did not participate in these activities and I did not ask you whether you participated in it, but you know of it, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, concerning Exhibit D2/59, when asked questions about that document, you said that it came from the counter-intelligence agency of the Republic of Croatia. So which of the intelligence agencies did you obtain that document from? If it assists you, perhaps if necessary --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday. I don't need the document. I was very clear yesterday. I told you exactly what the name of that service was, and you repeated it, didn't you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the correct name of the agency is -- the Counter-intelligence Agency of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I was clear yesterday. The Counter-intelligence Service of the Republic of Croatia. It is the former service for the protection of the constitutional order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't, of course, be able to say it in Croatian, but formerly known as the HDZ SUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the former abbreviation. Now it is POA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you used the term yesterday historiography, and can you tell the Chamber what that means or at least how you used that phrase?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's put it this way: It is a very unclear term in the circles, in the circles that I belong to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you used the term, unless I misheard you. What does that term mean to you?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Critical analysis of history, i.e. documents or, to be more precise, sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, again that you testified yesterday that you've looked at this history of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in your words, from the Croatian point of view? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that what I said was that I studied some segments of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the Croatian point of view.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which involved Croatians. I believe that I said that it had to do with the share of Croats in that war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the report that you did and which has been provided to the Chamber, have you been paid or compensated by anyone to prepare that report?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you prepare that report, sir, in your private capacity as a private individual or have you submitted this in some fashion representing some political group or some part of the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I prepared the study at the request of Mr. Seric and Mr. Par with the verbal approval of the head of my institute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did it nobly, perhaps. You did this work for free. You weren't compensated for your time or the effort that you went in to preparing this some 22 pages of text and another 20 pages of footnotes. Is that what you're telling us, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not my free time. It was during my working hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this work was supported, then, to answer my question about whether it was in your private capacity or some other capacity, you did this report while being employed by and on the time off of the Croatian Institute of History, which is an entity of the Republic of Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Institute for Croatian History is an institution, not an entity. I told you yesterday that I work on the project of the homeland Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. war and the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who funds the Croatian Institute of History? Who provides the operating funds, pays the electric bills?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institute pays.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The institute obtains its funds from where?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I answered that question 15 minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've described the war in Bosnia yesterday as a war about territory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I heard you well yesterday, you said that this process of disintegration of Bosnia-Herzegovina is in fact not yet complete; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, you've made it clear in both your report and in your testimony yesterday that, in fact, you consider that the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina is not over, is it?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said on page 1 of your report, for instance, that the conflicts between the three main groups continues and was not solved by Dayton now, was this reflected in the fact by Mr. Ante Jelavic, for instance, who had been the Bosnian-Croat member of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was removed by the office of the High Representative for advocating and taking steps to create a separate Croat entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I told you yesterday that I do not study Bosnia and Herzegovina after the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you've told us that the war is going on. In fact, you said yesterday that the protectorate of the international community prevents Bosnia and Herzegovina's disappearance and most probably a new war; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously you only hear things that you want to hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in fact, sir, I read the transcript last night, and I think at 9.54 yesterday, that's what you said, and it can certainly be checked. So I'm wondering, sir, you've worked in this institute, you've worked since the 1980s for, or in association, with the Croatian government. If the war is not over, sir, which side are you on?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was very clear when I said that the Dayton Accords interrupted the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, that Bosnia and Herzegovina has been divided. That is now a protectorate of the international community, and that in -- bearing in mind the previous phenomena, the previous occurrences, it will not be a theatre of war for as long as members of the armed forces of the international community are present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I repeat my question to you. If the war is not over, which you say it is not, which side are you on?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the war was interrupted. There is a difference between something being interrupted and something being over, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, we have your report and we'll go forward. Now, in response to questions by Mr. Krsnik yesterday, you seem to indicate, again if I heard you, that there is no government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I please hear the recording of that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't -- that's up to the President, of course, Witness. I'm in the President's hands. It it's not up to me to answer that, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Krsnik, you could ask your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I remember it very clearly, but I'm also familiar with the method of the cross-examination by my learned friend to the question whether there is a Bosnia and Herzegovinian government. The witness replied very clearly that he doesn't study Bosnia and Herzegovina after the Dayton and that he cannot answer that question. I believe I remember that very well, and you, Mr. President, I believe you listened very carefully to both my answer and the witness's -- both my question and the witness's answer and that you will remember that. But my learned friend uses his well-known rhetorics in his cross-examination, and I'm sure we will hear all sorts of questions coming from him today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it is a very, very simple question. We don't need the expertise of this witness to answer this question. Maybe, Mr. Scott, you can ask this question again to see how this witness will answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I will not engage in colloquy with the counsel at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it not -- were not the questions put to you yesterday afternoon -- morning I suppose it was, questions about whether there were in fact anything to be considered a government of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Do you remember that series of questions from Mr. Krsnik? Do you remember saying essentially "no"?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you have in mind specifically? Yesterday we mentioned the government in several different frameworks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I just -- one question, and we could ask several, but there are international embassies, agencies and organisations in Bosnia-Herzegovina even as we speak today that deal every day with government agencies representing Bosnia and Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there is a huge presence of representatives of various international organisations in Bosnia. They are so numerous that one cannot fail to see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they deal every day, sir, don't they, with agencies and departments and representatives of the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not work in the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is what you say. It may be true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me put my case to you very plainly. As an historian, sir, you appear to have antipathy towards Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Muslims or Bosniaks. Your report suggests that the Bosnia-Herzegovina has never been a "real country." The Muslims have near really been a "real nation" in the sense that you understand or use that word; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not only object, I protest. This is an insult to my witness's address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the Prosecutor just quoted his own report, and the witness has the free will to say yes or no, whether he mentioned in his report that Bosnia-Herzegovina has never been a real country. These are facts that everybody can look to in that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. My learned friend said that the witness appears to have antipathy towards Bosnia and Herzegovina. Why doesn't he ask very clear, very correct questions if he wants to continue this cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I put the Prosecution case to the witness, and I think it's proper, and I think we should have his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think there is some sense, you know, in the objections from Mr. Seric. You shouldn't use that antipathy towards Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Muslims or Bosniaks. Just ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will rephrase it, Your Honour, if it will assist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it is your view, as stated in your paper and the crux of your testimony, or at least a part of it, that Bosnia-Herzegovina has never been a "real country" and the Muslims have never been a "real nation," so the positions that they took and the things that happened during the war by either the Serbs on the one hand or the Croats on the other were justified?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that your interpretation is very liberal and that it goes to the extent of insults. The question that you have asked me, I can tell you that this is not what I said, firstly. Do you understand the chronological depth of this issue, of this question? Bear in mind the years, the time. I do not think you have to put it to me and tell me that I said something that I didn't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if that's not your position, sir, is it your position that the Muslim or Bosniak nation has the same or equal rights as the Croats, had the same rights to organise and defend themselves, had the same rights to take political action, had the same rights to negotiate with enemies such as the Serbs, or were those rights that only the Croats had?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the rights to defend themselves that belonged to Croats belonged equally to Muslims during the war. However, there are usually no rights in any war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is a banovina, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A banovina is an administrative unit which existed on the territory of Croatia, of the medieval Croatia, the medieval Bosnia, and in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At page 2 of your report, sir, you mention that the Croatian banovina was established, at least on another occasion if not previously, in 1939 [RealTime transcript read in error"1933"]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was the banovina of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown two exhibits, please, 899 and 862. Mr. President, if we could finish with these exhibits, then perhaps we could take the break. If those could be placed on the ELMO, please, that would be helpful. Perhaps we could start with Exhibit 899. It may be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the record, this is the line 22 -- [In English] Page 22, line 17. [Interpretation] The year is 1933 and it should have been the year 1939. So can we correct that in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'd look first of all, sir, at the coloured copy, do you see there in what would be the boldest, kind of a reddish orange colour, wrapping around what might be described as a pink area in the middle. Does that show what would be called the Croatian banovina in 1939, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, I simply provided 862 as well in the case that one or the other might be more helpful. The smaller insert map on 862 perhaps shows it in that scale quite clearly as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also say, sir -- I'm sorry. We can stop there, Mr. President, if you like?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's time for a vehicle. We will resume at a quarter to four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before we continue on, it was -- someone pointed out to me during the break that a name of a person you gave earlier, we may not have gotten it correctly in the transcript or it's quite possible -- possible that we did, but just in case. When you described or identified the person who was the commander of the 1st HVO Guards Brigade, is that a man named Zeljko Vlasnovic [As interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Zeljko Glasnovic, so once again it is misspelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so we don't come back to it, can you spell the last name for the record, please? If you can.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should be G rather than V in the last name. It is G-L-A-S-N-O-V-I-C.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we were talking before the break about the banovina, the Croatian banovina. You say in your report at page 2 that the Croatian banovina was expanded during World War II under the name of something called the Independent State of Croatia or NDH; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the NDH and how was that established?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Independent State of Croatia is -- was a state which was founded by Germany and Italy after breaking apart the Kingdom of Yugoslavia in April 1941.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you still have or if the usher can assist us if you don't, if you still have Exhibit 899 available to you. Could you please use that map to show Their Honours, the Judges, the boundaries of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Independent State of Croatia during World War II.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, say the eastern border moved to the River Drina and another part in the area of Dalmatia has shrunk in favour of Italy, and a part of Medjimurje in favour of Hungary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, so we can help make the record clear, can you take, if you can, please, take the pointer, can you trace for the Judges the Drina River that you say would have been the eastern -- approximately the eastern border?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forgive me, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's here. This is Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that time, the Independent State of Croatia included essentially all the pink area in the middle of Exhibit 899 and additional territory that would have been to the east; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And a part of East Herzegovina down to the border with Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on page 2 of your report you also say that after World War II, the borders of the Independent State of Croatia were then reduced again. And were they reduced again to what we see in the orange red on the exhibit or what were the borders of the Croatian banovina after World War II?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you again are seeing something that nobody else does. Where do you see that I -- where do you see the Independent State of Croatia after World War II? Perhaps it wouldn't be bad if you read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've read your report, sir, I can assure you, several times. In the first paragraph on the top of page 2, you say: "Upon the end of World War II, the borders were drawn back with minor corrections to correspond with the time of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy. So can you show us on this map what were the borders of the Croatian banovina after World War II?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you frankly, I am not much of a geographer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. We'll move on. Another part of Bosnia-Herzegovina that you mention in your report is called the Posavina. Now, can the usher show you Exhibit P3.5. It's another map. It may be loose. You can use mine. It should be in the first binder, the overall exhibit binders, but in any event, if could you put that on the ELMO, please. Sir, is this an exhibit a map marked as Exhibit 3.5, the area that is in green, as opposed to grey, does that correctly show what you've described in your paper as the Bosnian Posavina?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, around the same time that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was declared in 1991, was there not also another entity declared called the Croatian Community of the Bosnian Posavina or Bosanska Posavina?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So isn't it correct, sir, that what was -- what was established as the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in many ways paralleled territory claimed and that was one time part of the Croatian banovina and the part claimed by the Croatian Community of the Bosanska Posavina was the green part shown on this map 3.5; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pretty correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the first democratic multi-party elections we all know and you say in your report were held on the 18th of November, 1990, and you say that the nationalist parties won overwhelmingly. And just so we're clear, sir, when you say nationalist parties, you include the HDZ; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes. The HDZ, SDA, and the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you talk about the HDZ political party in Bosnia-Herzegovina, this was really a branch of the HDZ party that had -- was first established in Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd put it in a different way. I'd say, rather, that their political goals were similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that the HDZ party in Bosnia-Herzegovina, for all practical purposes, was an extension of the HDZ political party founded by Franjo Tudjman and others in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This claim is very widespread. But personally, I've seen too little evidence to corroborate it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, is it correct and do you recall testifying yesterday that the Croatian -- the Croat Democratic Union as a Croat party advocated views identical to the views of the Croat democratic party? Do you recall that testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had the same view regarding the future of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And further, sir, you talk about various organisations in the course ever your cross-examination and in your report, for that matter, you identify the HVO or the Croatian Defence Council as being essentially part of the HDZ, in the same way that you equate the SDA with the ABiH; is that correct? One being a political party and one being a military and/or government organisation.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say, sir, that the war was instigated by the proponents of Greater Serbia expansionism. What do you mean by "Greater Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The expansion of the borders of the Republic of Serbia to border areas of the Republic of Croatia where the Serbs were a majority population, that is, to the Virovitica, Karlovac, Karlobag line. Everything east of it was to become part of Greater Serbia, that is, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say at page 2 of your report that the Serb party, the political party in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or the SDS, was nationalistic and centrally connected to Belgrade, and the SDS wanted to merge with the parent nation Serbia. Now, how do you mean and in what ways was it centrally connected to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To begin with, I did not say it was nationalistic, but that doesn't matter. It was a link which linked Serbia and Croatia, that is, Serb areas in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me restate. Perhaps I wasn't clear. And if I wasn't, I apologise. I believe you say in your paper that the Serb political party the SDS was centrally connected to Belgrade. I'd like for you to explain for the Judges in what way you mean that that political party was connected to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to say here that I wrote "a connective tissue," as said. That is not quite one and the same thing. I wanted to say, and it can be proven, too, that those two parties in Serbia, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, I mean Serb parties, and the Serb party in Croatia, were subordinated to the policy laid down in Belgrade, something about that. I read something about that in a text, about the role of the Yugoslav People's Army, of course supported by evidence in the war against the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, wasn't the HDZ political party in Bosnia-Herzegovina the Bosnian Croat party, just in the same way centrally connected, or to use your word, had connective tissues to the HDZ party in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that one can draw a mark of equality between the two, because it was very, very clear. The Serbs were very clear about that, what they did in Croatia between 1990/1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a matter of fact or is it a matter of clarity, sir? Are you simply saying the Serbs were simply more overt about their programme and plans than the Croats were?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't really put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say in your paper that on the 24th of October, 1991, the Bosnian-Herzegovnian Serbs started -- excuse me -- disintegration of Bosnia and Herzegovina by founding the assembly of the Serb people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And further that on the 21st of December, 1991, they issued the "Decision on constituting the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again in order to try to move forward a bit in time, that is in the time we have in the courtroom, let me see if I understand your position on another topic. Do you suggest or is it the position that you take in your paper that because Bosnian Muslims, who happened to be or were on active duty at the time in the JNA and fought then in the JNA units against Croats in Croatia, and because JNA or Serb forces attacked -- attacking Croatia operated from Bosnia and Herzegovina as bases and because the Bosnian Muslims engaged in what you described as a "pro-Yugoslavian neutrality," that it is your proposition or thesis that Bosnia-Herzegovina engaged in a war against Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But you forgot the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by the Territorial Defence, are you talking about the Territorial Defence at the time it was part of the JNA or after a new Territorial Defence was established by Bosnia and Herzegovina in approximately April 1992?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence was never, in no way, belonged to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It existed, sir, under the military structure of the former Yugoslavia; correct? It existed in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. As a part of the armed forces of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it further correct, sir, as I read your paper at page 3, that you contend that since Muslim TO forces were being paid by the budget of another state, in this case you say Bosnia, that therefore in fighting on the side of the Serbs, again it's your contention that this amounted to Bosnia-Herzegovina engaging in war against Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd -- I'd like to give a slightly broader answer to your question. We have already said that the territory, the area is used for the attack, that a part of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina is used. And I think that it suffices for the claim that Bosnia-Herzegovina participated in the aggression against the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it your contention, sir, that in the way that you've described to the Chamber in your report and just now, is it your contention then that that made the Serb attacks on Croatia or the fighting in Croatia an international armed conflict involving Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once again it depends on how you treat the dissolution of Yugoslavia. I think -- well, perhaps I won't be quite accurate here. The thesis of the French lawyer Badinter is accepted, that Yugoslavia fell apart in June 1991, and that, I guess, meant that we were dealing with an international conflict there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, on page 3, the end of the next to last paragraph on page 3 of your report, at the last sentence of that paragraph, did you not say: "Is it not consistent then to state that BiH committed aggression against the Republic of Croatia?" That's the position stated in your paper. Now, are you changing your position today?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not changing your position.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that in the -- in an earlier period of the conflict, of these events, the Croatians unsuccessfully were -- excuse me -- were unsuccessfully trying to reach an agreement with Serbs on the ceasefire and demarcation, and then you go on to say that there were several meetings of the leaders of Bosnian Serbs and Croats outside Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992, which achieved no concrete results. Can you tell us some of the meetings between the Bosnian Serbs and Croats that you had in mind when you wrote that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the visit of Nikola Koljevic in Zagreb, I believe sometime in February 1992, and the meeting in Graz in May 1992, a meeting of Mate Boban and Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's helpful, sir, because to be perfectly transparent, I was not clear from your report whether you agreed that the meetings in Graz occurred or if you were denying that they had occurred. So you agree that Radovan Karadzic and Mate Boban had talks about the settlement of the war and the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Graz about May of 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They talked, and all the dailies carried a press release, and in it one could see that they had failed to reach an understanding on a demarcation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't it be fair to say, sir, that they agreed on some things but to use the phrase then "Agreed to disagree on other things"? Is that an accurate statement?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say I wasn't there. I only know what I read in the papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, in that regard, sir, can the usher please assist us in showing the witness Exhibit 126.1, which should be in the first Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. bundle. Mr. President, I should have explained at the beginning and I apologise, with this witness, two bundles -- actually, three bundles have been prepared. The first smaller bundle is a set of documents that will be at this first -- that relates to the first part of this examination, and I hope that they were pretty much in the order in which they would come up in the examination and that is a first bundle would include 126.1. There is then a much thicker bundle, a second bundle, and then I'm afraid, as testimony went yesterday, then there is a third bundle which didn't get integrated into the two existing sets because they'd already been -- were already substantially under preparation, but I'll try to assist the Chamber as much as possible in directing you to the correct documents. But, sir, if you look at Exhibit P126.1, you said there was a press release, and indeed do you recall seeing what's marked here or hearing about -- you can certainly look at it for a moment, that this being the gist, if you will, about what was reported about the meetings between Mr. Boban and Mr. Karadzic in Graz in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that my English is not very good. Can I have this in the original language?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies, sir. It hasn't been provided to you, and if we still have time before you finish, I'll try to see if I can provide it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, to be fair to the witness, would you please read the certain paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That is what I was just looking at. It's hard to pick out any one particular sentence, Mr. President. I apologise. Without reading the entire document. But let me read -- starting at the beginning of the page of the document over the written names of Radovan Karadzic and Mate Boban. It would be the second page of the exhibit. It says this: "Our intention being to resolve peacefully by agreement all outstanding issues including the borderline between our two constituent units, the Croatian unit and the Serbian unit, in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The representatives of the Croatian and the Serbian national communities have established the existing -- existence of the following specific differences as regards the working demarcation map: Number 1, in the city of Mostar, the Serbian side considers the Neretva River to be the borderline, while the Croatian side considers the entire city of Mostar to be within the Croatian constituent unit. Number 2, south of Mostar, the Croatian side considers the entire area delineated in 1939, in other words, the borders of the Hrvatska banovina to be in the Croatian constituent unit. The Serbian side considers the Neretva River to be the borderline between the Croatian and the Serbian constituent units." Now, let me stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you -- as an historian and from what you heard at the time, is that what you recall?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document. Summaries, I've already told you, appeared in the press, but can you please continue reading this document? Let's see who the organisers of this meeting were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I can refer, Mr. Marijan, without reading the entire document, I think it's fair to say that the negotiations were to some extent encouraged by the European Community, if that's what you're getting at. Is that what you're trying to suggest, which I'm prepared to say that that's correct, but is that what you're trying to get at?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. And if I may say another thing, I would like to repeat what I said yesterday several times, and I've already said it today, and that is something that you insisted upon at the beginning. There is the influence of the international community everywhere. The international community has always been designing maps. It has always continuously divided Bosnia and Herzegovina, and eventually it has managed to divide Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Dayton Accords. Now, I'm not clear that I understand what you are trying to prove talking about a failed -- the failed Croatian attempt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think I said anything about a failed Croatian attempt, but let's move on, sir, because as I said a few moments ago, I was not clear from your report whether you in fact simply denied that Graz had occurred at all. That appears to be not your position. Moving forward, then, sir --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please tell me -- I apologise. Can you please tell me where it was that I denied it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I won't get into extensive discussions with you, but if I can do it very quickly, I will tell you that.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you where you may have found the place where you thought that I denied it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just so you --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I commented upon Mr. Izetbegovic's attitude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I think, and so the record's clear and so the Judges can be advised if it's something they want to look at, it's page 21 of the report. Perhaps it's a translation issue, sir, and I -- as I said several times, I was not clear what your position was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe it would be fair if such allegations are not given without giving the witness the opportunity to explain, because this is not the witness's position. It is something that is alleged by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, at this moment I cannot find this part. I commented upon the recollections of Mr. Izetbegovic, who had placed this in April 1992, and that was clearly an attempt to justify his policy. Mr. Izetbegovic is a very important factor, because the other two leaders, one of them is dead and the other one is hiding. He is on a run. And this is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in the third paragraph, the third paragraph starting on page 21, not quite halfway down through the paragraph is this sentence -- it seems rather categorical: "It seems no evidence exists of the Karadzic-Boban talks and both participants denied them." So that is what caused me to think that you were denying that these negotiations ever occurred. But apparently as was indicated, that's not your position, and I appreciate the clarification.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true, sir, that after approximately June 1992, there was no significant sustained fighting between the Croats and Serbs in what might be described as the Prozor-Mostar-Stolac region for the remainder of 1992 and all of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The end of March 1992, the fighting started in Bosanska Posavina, and this fighting ended by the fall of Bosanski Brod on the 6th of October, 1992. The 101st Brigade of the HVO had some 400 dead during the -- these fightings. To my mind, it is a lot. And it talks about the extent of that fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't want to interrupt you, but that was not my question. I wasn't talking about Bosanski Brod. I was talking about the region as I described it, the approximate zone running from Prozor, south to Mostar, south to Stolac. In that region, sir, after approximately June 1992, there was no significant fighting between Croats and Serbs, at least until sometime in 1994; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian forces entered Stolac in June 1992. In June, they were the so-called "June Dawns" around Mostar. In July of the same year, Serbs had a counter -- launched a counter-attack in the area of Mostar. And in November, there was the Operation Bura at the foot of the mountain Velez. In other words, there was some fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true and don't you state at page 9 of your report that by the end of 1992 at least and with the fall of Jajce and the Bosnian Posavina, the Bosnian Croats and Serbs had reached a stalemate; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not -- it was not a ceasefire but what we actually call a stalemate. There was still gunfire, shelling. The daily report coming from the operation zone of Northwest Herzegovina are available to you, and you can read in those reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, any violence, of course, is too much, and there were certainly skirmishes and artillery shells fired from time to time, but isn't it true, sir, that in 1993 in the Prozor-Mostar-Stolac region fighting between Serbs and Croats was not a significant factor in what was happening there?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I'd like the witness to please be shown Exhibit 126.11. 126.11, which is a map, multicoloured map, in the first bundle, I hope. Or it's loose. I'm told it's in the loose set. Sorry. If it's easier, you can use mine. Thank you. If that could just be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a map that's been prepared that -- giving in one -- in the blue colour the area that you described today when you said that the Serbs started the war by declaring the Serb republic, a Republika Srpska, and the area claimed then by -- to be Herceg-Bosna, and the area with the blue and green vertical lines being the area of overlap. Isn't it true, sir, that in reality the areas of contention between the Serbs, on the one hand, and the Croats, on the other, were in fact quite limited?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct, Mr. Prosecutor. I will illustrate that by my own example. On the 13th of April, 1992, I was a member of the HVO in Koricina. That is a pass between Livno and Glamoc. On that day, the Tactical Group number 1 of the Knin Corps tried to enter Livno. They lost a tank and 20 men. A few kilometres further down west in the area called Strumica. They repeated the attempt. Again they lost a tank and a few men. Ten days later, another attempt was made, and this time from the direction of Bosansko Grahovo. They lost three tanks, an armoured vehicle, some 30 men. You can read about that in greater detail in a report written by General Slavko Lisica in his memoirs. Maybe it wouldn't be a bad idea for you to read such literature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate that, sir. I'm not suggesting that these lines were ever exactly achieved and that there weren't areas of contention otherwise but simply the areas claimed by the Serbs and the areas claimed by the Bosnian Croats on the 18th of November, 1991, when they declared the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, that if each side got exactly what they wanted, there wouldn't have been that much in contention; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are trying exactly what I just said. You have your own picture. You are not interested in the facts. You are putting things out of the context and in a certain way you've been insulting me, sir. On the 13th of April, I almost lost my life, and I'm not in no way in the mood for your very imaginative way of putting things to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the Croats were left out of the various negotiations between the Bosnian Muslims and the Serbs, at page 8 of your report. And you say that these negotiations between Muslims and Serbs ended in June of 1992 in failure.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic writes about that in his memoirs, and he does it really very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report, sir, you're critical -- one of the criticisms you direct toward the Bosnian side is they engaged in negotiations with the Serbs without the presence of the Croats. My question to you, sir, is didn't the Croats do exactly the same thing including at Graz between Mate Boban and Karadzic with no Muslims there?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly when you say the Bosnian side?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The central government you might call it. The BiH Presidency. I think you know well, sir. You're an historian and you know which of the three parties I'm referring to. Why is it, sir, that it's your contention that the Croats were entitled to have their separate meetings with the Serbs but you won't give that same right to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please allow after the question of the witness, when the -- when the witness says the Bosnian side and asks what does the Prosecutor mean by that, can we allow the witness to answer that, what he means by the Bosnian side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The country that we see in front of us on the screen is not Bosnia. It is not its name. Its name is Bosnia and Herzegovina. Please, Mr. Prosecutor, bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, throughout your 22-page report you repeatedly use the word" Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. "Muslim" and in a few instances "Bosniak." Now, you know exactly which group I'm referring to; don't you?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a mind reader. But I would like to answer your previous question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that Mr. Izetbegovic negotiated under the patronage of the international community with the staff of the Supreme Command of the socialist federative Republic of Yugoslavia. The meeting of -- in Graz was organised by the international community, and you seem to be forgetting that all the time. It was the gentlemen from Europe who invited them. And the story started in Portugal, in Lisbon. And it ended, as I've already said, by the Dayton Accords, by the division of this country that I see in front of me on the screen, the country that was divided by the international community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I think we understand from your testimony yesterday and today that you blame the international community, in part, for the war. We understand that. Needless --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the key culprit, to my mind. Even bigger than the Serbs themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It allowed the Serbian war machine to go on a rampage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Needless to say --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it's still recognised this area that has been ethnically cleansed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Be that as it may, sir, you're not willing to extend the same right to the Muslims to negotiate and have discussions with one or the other warring parties to the same extent that the Croats claimed that right for themselves; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your conclusion, and it is not correct, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said already who the organisers of Graz were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we can't stay on this longer. Your report's in evidence and certainly can be quoted later. You say that the big problem in Bosnia and Herzegovina was the parallel political and military structures between the Bosnian Croats, or HVO, on the one side and the Muslims, or ABiH, on the other side, at page 13. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what parallel structures exactly do you have in mind when you make this -- when you state this thesis?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian and the Muslim, which from 1994 has been the Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in terms of parallel political and military structures, to use your terms, you're talking about the HVO government on the one side and the BiH Presidency on the other side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are talking about the HVO government. That is the HDZ government, to be more precise and more honest, and the SDA government in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me understand. Between these two parallel structures, as you say, do you recall that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was recognised as a sovereign state by the European Community on the 6th of April, 1992? Can you please tell the Judges on what date the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was recognised as a state by the European Community?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the -- at the moment when it was involved in the negotiations about the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's your position that the European Community at some point recognised that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was a state?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as a state but as an equal participant and an equal negotiator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, they were one of the warring parties. Wasn't it essential that the international negotiators had to negotiate with all three sides whether they recognised any of them as being legitimate or not; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be correct. However, we across -- we are talking at cross-purposes. You don't want to seem to understand me. It would be so if the representatives of the international community had not created Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of the parallel structure, sir, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was admitted as a member state of the United Nations on the 22nd of May, 1992. Can you tell the Judges, please, when the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was admitted as a member state of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR MARIJAN [Resumed]
